tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact required format. The scorer extracts the last parseable list, so the answer must be a well‑formed list of [disk, from, to] triples.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you have generated the full move sequence and are ready to output the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing moves as plain text or using parentheses instead of brackets, causing the parser to fail to read a valid list.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk you need to move is not the topmost disk on its peg, first relocate any smaller disks that are on top of it to other pegs. This clears the larger disk for a legal move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before attempting to move a larger disk that has smaller disks above it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to move disk 3 while disk 2 remains on top, resulting in a source‑peg mismatch.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Check that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg; moving any other disk violates the rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 3 from a peg where disk 2 is on top, causing an illegal source selection.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk; otherwise a larger‑on‑smaller placement occurs.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, which is illegal because 2 < 4.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When you need to transfer a contiguous stack of k disks from one peg to another using the third peg as a buffer, recursively move the top k‑1 disks, move the kth disk, then move the k‑1 disks onto it.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a clean stack of consecutive disks must be moved as a unit.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move a three‑disk stack without recursively handling the sub‑stack, resulting in missing intermediate moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg currently holds smaller disks that must end up above the larger disk in the final configuration, move those smaller disks elsewhere first.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Before moving a larger disk onto a peg that already contains smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 sits on top, which would block the correct final ordering.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal‑first descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the goal is to stack all disks on a single peg, prioritize moving the largest remaining disk that can be placed correctly before handling smaller ones.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: In goal‑oriented tasks where the final stack occupies one peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing a small disk onto the target peg before the larger disk that should be below it, later causing an illegal placement.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state to verify that the final configuration matches the goal; this catches missing or illegal moves that individual checks might miss.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After generating the full move sequence, before outputting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg, which passes per‑move checks but fails the overall goal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use the smallest disk as a flexible temporary placeholder
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Treat the smallest disk (disk 1) as a universal temporary buffer; it can be placed on any larger disk or an empty peg to free up other pegs for larger moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need a temporary holder to free larger disks or to rearrange order.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Failing to move disk 1 to a free peg, which leaves a larger disk blocked and prevents progress.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Make move list the final parseable list
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Place the move list as the very last list in the response and avoid any additional brackets, lists, or text after it; the scorer reads the last parseable list as the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When outputting the final answer; after the move list, output nothing else.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Appending an empty list [] after the correct move list, causing the parser to read the empty list as the answer and reject it.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the puzzle is already solved or may truncate output before any moves are emitted.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always generate at least one move when the initial state differs from the goal, and verify that the move list is not empty before output.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of space or stops early, cutting off the sequence before reaching the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the solution within the token budget, keep the move sequence concise, and double‑check that the final configuration is reached.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to verify that the chosen disk is the topmost one on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate the source peg's top disk matches the intended disk before each move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model neglects to compare the size of the moving disk with the top disk on the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Validate that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk before each move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Extra list after move list causing parser to read wrong answer
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model includes stray brackets or an additional list after the correct move list, so the scorer extracts the last list (often empty) as the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Ensure the move list is the final parseable list in the response; do not output any further lists or characters after it.
